newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek brokers rep says row over bourse bill over.
newsitem.headline: Greek brokers rep says row over bourse bill over.

text.p: Greek National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou has agreed to drop a phrase from a draft bill that risked stirring protests by Athens Stock Exchange brokers, the president of the brokers' association said.

Panagiotis Kondalexis, after meeting Papandoniou, told Reuters: "The situation (at the bourse) is being normalised. The contentious item in the draft bill will be withdrawn. We will not have any resignations from the guarantee fund board."
Funds from the clearing house and the brokers' guarantee fund were expected to be used this week to cover a 2.6 billion drachma default by Delta Securities, he said.
Delta's attempt to cover its balance at the clearing house with bad cheques triggered a crisis 10 days ago which shut down most trading at the bourse for four days.

On Friday, four of the guarantee fund's five board members had threatened to resign over the draft bill which they said would sidestep a deal between brokers and the government to pay for Delta's default.
They were in disagreement over an article of the draft bill that appeared to allow the clearing house to avoid paying its part of the default.
Article A, paragraph two in the draft bill stated that "the guarantee fund must 'submit funds immediately' to the clearing house", prompting the disagreement with the ministry.
Kondalexis said it was agreed that the phrase "submit funds immediately" would be taken out of the draft bill.
He will update brokers' association members on his meeting with Papandoniou at 1430 local (1230 GMT).
Papandoniou and Kondalexis also agreed on a closer working relationship between the brokers and the ministry in the future, he said.
A national economy ministry spokesman told Reuters there would be an announcement on Tuesday or Wednesday. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
